New research reveals the strongest solar event ever detected, in 12350 BC
by
University of Oulu
Credit:
Earth and Planetary Science Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1016/j.epsl.2025.119383
An international team of scientists has discovered an extreme spike in radiocarbon corresponding to the year 12350 BC during the dusk of the last Ice Age. However, the strength of the event could not be assessed earlier because of the lack of an appropriate model. It has now been identified as the most powerful solar particle storm known to date—a colossal space weather storm that struck Earth 14,300 years ago. This recent finding expands the timeline and intensity of known solar activity and sets a new upper boundary for such solar phenomena.
In the study, postdoctoral researcher Kseniia Golubenko and Professor Ilya Usoskin at the University of Oulu, Finland, used their newly developed chemistry–climate model called SOCOL:14C-Ex, specifically designed to reconstruct solar particle storms under ancient glacial climate conditions.
The model confirmed that the detected solar event was approximately 18% stronger than the notorious AD 775 event—until now the strongest solar
storm
ever recorded in tree-ring archives. The work is
published
in the journal
Earth and Planetary Science Letters
.
"Compared to the largest event of the modern satellite era—the 2005 particle storm—the ancient 12350 BC event was over 500 times more intense, according to our estimates," says Dr. Golubenko.
Other large known solar particle storms have occurred around 994 AD, 663 BC, 5259 BC and 7176 BC, and a few other candidates are under investigation. The new model was also verified using wood samples recently found in the French Alps, dating back some 14,300 years.
Solar particle storms are rare, but when they occur, they bombard Earth with an enormous amount of high-energy particles. In comparison, the famous Carrington event in 1859 was a different kind of event and not accompanied by a solar particle storm.
"The ancient event in 12350 BC is the only known extreme solar particle event outside of the Holocene epoch, the past ~12,000 years of stable warm climate," says Golubenko. "Our new model lifts the existing limitation to the Holocene and extends our ability to analyze radiocarbon data even for glacial climate conditions."
In the study, Golubenko and Usoskin designed the SOCOL:14C-Ex model to assess the solar particle storm intensity under glacial conditions. The model was successfully validated using data in tree rings from the AD 775 event and applied to the late Ice Age conditions to study the 12350 BC event.
With the model, the researchers assessed the strength, timing, and terrestrial effects of the most extreme solar particle event presently known. The
model
—now validated under both Holocene and glacial conditions—marks a major step forward in analyzing radiocarbon variations across different climatic and geomagnetic epochs.
The international research team included scientists from France and Switzerland, and was led by Professor Edouard Bard from CEREGE, France.
A new era for radiocarbon dating—and worst-case scenario for solar storms
Solar particle storms can greatly enhance the normal production of cosmogenic isotopes like radiocarbon (
14
C) in the atmosphere by galactic cosmic rays. Such enhanced production, preserved in annual tree rings, serves as a clear cosmic timestamp making possible absolute dating of tree samples.
Such dramatic spikes—known as Miyake events, named after the Japanese researcher who first discovered them—offer invaluable data for scientists studying both
solar activity
, ancient Earth systems and space climate.
"Miyake events allow us to pin down exact calendar years in floating archaeological chronologies," says Usoskin. Radiocarbon signals from such events have already enabled researchers to precisely date Viking settlements in Newfoundland and Neolithic communities in Greece.
The findings revise our understanding of solar physics and space weather extremes. "This event establishes a new
worst-case scenario
," Golubenko notes. "Understanding its scale is critical for evaluating the risks posed by future solar storms to modern infrastructure like satellites, power grids, and communication systems."

(2025).

data.title: America's College Towns Go from Boom to Bust
data.author: JumpCrisscross
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：高等教育院校，尤其是二三线院校面临的经济困境及其未来发展方向

不同观点：
• [decimalenough] 认为标题具有误导性。文章指出，大型旗舰大学依然在推动地方经济发展，但位于经济落后地区的二三线院校（如文中提到的西伊利诺伊大学麦克omb校区）正面临困境。由于这些学校的学历价值不高且无法提供本地就业机会，学生不愿意支付高昂学费。

• [mjevans] 总结文章内容，指出大学入学率下降的原因包括出生率下降、大学投资回报率下降、联邦资金削减等。同时提出，关闭多余的学校是必然的，应重新利用这些资源。建议简化大学课程设置，并提出加强职业教育，如技工、电工等职业，认为这些职业同样有需求且可以通过技术改进减少职业伤害。

• [keiferski] 建议三线院校转型为以职业教育为主的学校，吸引那些原本计划上大学但不考虑传统职业教育的学生。认为这种结合“大学体验”和职业教育的模式会有市场需求。

• [timr] 认为十多年前的人口趋势已经预示了当前的问题，大学在婴儿潮的最后回声中过度投资，导致如今的困境。

• [rekenaut] 指出，学生在选择较小学校时必须考虑学校是否能在四年后依然存在。随着越来越多私立和公立学院的关闭，学生会更倾向于选择州立旗舰大学。

补充讨论：
• 职业教育与传统大学教育的结合：[keiferski] 和 [mjevans] 都提到了职业教育的重要性，并建议将其与大学体验结合，以满足市场需求。
• 学校资源的重组与转型：[mjevans] 和 [timr] 都讨论了关闭多余学校和重新利用资源的必要性，提出了对教育资源进行重组的建议。
• 学校存续的不确定性：[rekenaut] 强调了学生在选择院校时面临的学校存续风险，这可能会进一步推动学生流向大型旗舰大学。

争议焦点：
• 二三线院校的未来发展方向：各方对如何解决二三线院校的经济困境存在不同看法，包括关闭学校、转型职业教育等。
• 大学教育的价值与回报：对大学教育的投资回报率存在争议，部分人认为职业教育可能是更好的选择。

data.article_summary: 本文列出了截至2025年5月18日美国高薪远程软件工程师（SWE）职位。岗位按公司、职位、工作经验、总薪酬和基本工资等信息分类。微软（Microsoft）、Coinbase、Airbnb和Reddit等知名公司提供了多个高薪远程职位。例如，微软的首席软件工程师年薪高达322,000美元，而Reddit的广告创意高级软件工程师年薪为507,000美元。Airbnb和Coinbase的多个职位年薪也超过500,000美元。职位经验要求从0到15年不等，涵盖初级到高级岗位。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕一个工作聚合网站的各种反馈与讨论，包括远程工作、薪资水平、职位真实性以及技术实现等问题。

不同观点：
• [对远程工作的质疑] koliber指出，某些标记为“远程工作”的职位实际上要求在特定地点工作，且需要每周四天到办公室，表明该聚合网站需要进一步优化。
• [对薪资和职位头衔的质疑] Cthulhu_ 和 welder 都提到薪资与工作年限、职称不匹配的问题。Cthulhu_ 特别指出欧洲与美国之间的薪资差距，而 welder 则提到自己作为资深软件工程师，看到现在的薪资比五年前还低。
• [对职位真实性的质疑] elwebmaster 和 confidantlake 提出职位真实性的问题。elwebmaster 讽刺地提到可能会有大量假简历涌入，confidantlake 则指出“幽灵职位”的存在，即公司在裁员后仍发布招聘信息，可能并没有实际招聘需求。

补充讨论：
• [技术实现与功能建议] nico 对聚合网站的技术实现表示兴趣，并询问是否提供API以便接入自己的工具。dinkblam 和 bbstats 则提出了对网站命名和功能的建议，如增加排序和搜索功能。
• [对薪资计算的疑问] icameron 询问总薪酬（total compensation）的计算方式，因为某些职位的总薪酬远高于基础薪资，但在招聘启事中未具体说明。
• [对全球市场的需求] Guestmodinfo 和 najmlion 提到希望该网站能覆盖印度和欧洲等地区，指出这些地区用户对工作机会的需求，以及对高薪资的期望。
• [对用户体验的反馈] mixmastamyk 提到网站上的动画影响了使用体验，建议去除不必要的动画效果。
• [法律与版权问题] Havoc 关注聚合网站如何处理信息合法性问题，包括版权和所抓取网站的使用条款。

争议焦点：
• 远程工作的定义与实际要求不符，用户质疑聚合网站的优化程度。
• 薪资水平与工作年限、职位头衔的不匹配，尤其是跨地域（如美国与欧洲）的对比。
• 职位真实性存疑，尤其是裁员后仍发布招聘信息的现象。

data.title: Living beings emit a faint light that extinguishes upon death, study
data.author: pseudolus
data.article_summary: 一项新研究发现，所有生物体都会发出一种微弱的超弱光子发射（UPE）光，这种光在死亡后消失。加拿大卡尔加里大学的研究人员通过比较活体和死亡小鼠，发现活体小鼠的UPE强度显著高于刚死亡的小鼠。而在植物中，UPE的强度受温度变化、损伤和化学处理等压力因素的影响。UPE是由细胞代谢过程中产生的活性氧（ROS）引起的，适量的ROS是细胞应激反应的一部分，但过量则导致氧化应激并产生UPE。尽管UPE无法用肉眼观察到，但它在单细胞生物、细菌、植物、动物甚至人类中广泛存在。这项研究表明，UPE可以作为生物活力和应激反应的敏感指标，并可能应用于非侵入性的医学诊断和研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：生物光子（或超弱光子发射）的性质、来源及其可能的应用和意义。

不同观点：
• **xenadu02** 认为，生物光子的现象已经存在几十年，某些氧化反应会释放光，但关键问题是能否从这些光中提取出有用的信息。由于人体的不透明性，利用生物光子进行成像非常困难。呼吸停止和氧化反应减缓会导致光子发射减少。

• **taejavu** 提出疑问，电磁辐射在什么情况下不被视为光？因为所有有温度的物体都会辐射“光”，那么生物光子和普通黑体辐射有何区别？希望澄清长久以来的误解。

• **Waterluvian** 提到，超弱光子发射（UPE）根据压力因素（如温度变化、伤害、化学处理）变化。这与通过多光谱卫星数据检测农作物压力的远程 sensing 技术类似，并认为这是一个有趣的发现。

• **userbinator** 认为，UPE 是一种极低强度的自发光，部分属于红外光谱，另一部分属于紫外光。这类似于所有非零绝对温度物体发出的黑体辐射，死后的生物体冷却后辐射减少是显然的。

• **fennecbutt** 进一步质疑，是否生物光子发射仅仅是物体黑体辐射的一部分？

• **moralestapia** 认为，200-1000纳米的光谱范围与我们感知的光谱重叠，在特定黑暗环境下，某些敏感的人或动物可能看到这些光子发射。

补充讨论：
• **efnx** 和 **DiabloD3** 以调侃方式提及电影《铁血战士》中的热成像概念，暗示生物光子发射现象在流行文化中已有体现。

• **3oil3** 和 **lostmsu** 以幽默方式讨论生物光子是否与“气场”有关，以及实验是否在老鼠身上进行。

• **markhahn** 指出，有些人对此现象感到神秘，但从工程角度看，要成为信号，光不仅需要被接收到，还需有方向性。

• **OutOfHere** 提到，此讨论与之前的一个帖子重复，提供了一个参考链接。

争议焦点：
生物光子发射是否仅仅是黑体辐射的一部分，还是有更复杂或有用的生物信息可以提取。这涉及到生物光子的本质及其潜在应用价值。

Living beings emit a faint light that extinguishes upon death, according to a new study
by
Sanjukta Mondal
, Phys.org
Credit:
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.4c03546
The light of someone's life might not be just another person, but light in the literal sense. According to a recent study by researchers from University of Calgary, every living system emits light without requiring external excitation due to a biological phenomenon known as ultraweak photon emission (UPE).
In
mice
, UPE was linked to vitality as live mice emitted significantly higher UPE intensity compared to recently dead mice. In plants, however, UPE varied depending on exposure to stress factors like temperature changes, injury and chemical treatments, as
reported
in
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
.
Living organisms are compact biochemical labs where complex chemical reactions keep the system up and running. Cellular metabolism, a series of chemical reactions that fuel life-sustaining processes, produces a group of highly reactive oxygen-containing molecules produced as a natural byproduct called
reactive oxygen species
or ROS.
Studies suggest that ROS plays a central role in UPE. When organisms encounter stress, they activate biochemical pathways that generate ROS, which act as signaling molecules in the
cellular stress response
. However, excessive ROS production can lead to
oxidative stress
, overwhelming the cell's antioxidant defenses. This oxidative stress can induce electron excitation and transfer processes, ultimately resulting in UPE.
High-sensitivity EMCCD and CCD cameras for imaging UPE in dark, controlled environments. Credit:
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.4c03546
Unlike bioluminescence, which produces high-intensity light visible to the naked eye, UPE, also known as biophoton emission, is a spontaneous release of extremely low-intensity light that is invisible to the human eye and falls within the spectral range of 200–1,000 nm. This faint light has been detected in a wide range of life forms—from
single-celled organisms
and bacteria to plants, animals, and even humans.
Despite being so widely observed, not much is known about the impact of mortality and stress factors on UPE. Furthermore, the ability to monitor UPE in response to stress factors and injuries could be a powerful, non-invasive tool for diagnostics and medical research.
The researchers used advanced imaging techniques to explore the biological significance of UPE by directly comparing emissions in living versus dead animals, while also systematically visualizing the effects of temperature, injury, and chemical treatments on UPE in plants.
Effect of the temperature on the intensity of UPE in plants. Credit:
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025). DOI: 10.1021/acs.jpclett.4c03546
To carry out the experiments, the researchers designed ultradark enclosures to eliminate environmental light interference. They then used an Electron-Multiplying Charge-Coupled Device (EMCCD) camera for imaging plants and a Charge-Coupled Device (CCD) camera with IVIS system to image UPE changes in mice.
The results revealed that despite both groups having the same body temperature of 37°C, the live mice showed robust emissions, whereas the UPE from the euthanized mice was nearly extinguished. In plants, an increase in temperature and injuries led to an increase in UPE intensity. Injured sites were consistently brighter than uninjured parts—a change in the former was observed once the site received any chemical treatment.
This study establishes that UPE can act as a sensitive indicator of vitality in animals and of stress responses in plants. The researchers suggest that these findings could catalyze the application of UPE imaging as a non-invasive technique for both basic biological research and clinical diagnostics.
More information:
V. Salari et al, Imaging Ultraweak Photon Emission from Living and Dead Mice and from Plants under Stress,
The Journal of Physical Chemistry Letters
(2025).

data.title: Show HN: A Wolfenstein3D-like raycaster made in Windows Batch
data.author: nthornton
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由Windows Batch编写的类Wolfenstein3D的射线追踪项目（Batch Raycaster）。该项目在功能上模拟了老式的DDA射线追踪，尽管Batch不支持浮点运算和内置的三角函数。由于这些限制，生成一帧图像大约需要1.5秒，并且通过控制台输入进行移动。用户可以修改`map.txt`自定义地图，并通过运行`raycaster.bat`启动程序。提供优化版本`raycaster_optimized.bat`以提升性能，但代码可读性较差。项目基于MIT许可证，由Nikolas Thornton开发。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对Batch作为童年编程语言的看法

不同观点：
• [正面观点 - nootis] Batch作为童年的编程语言具有特殊意义。nootis表示Batch是他儿时想用来制作游戏的第一个"编程语言"，虽然当时没有实现制作游戏的梦想，但看到有人实现让他感到很酷。这表明Batch对他有情感价值，代表了一种童年梦想的延续。

• [质疑观点 - codingbot3000] codingbot3000对使用Batch作为童年编程语言表示疑问，带有些许调侃的语气（"why? :-D"），暗示可能对选择Batch作为游戏开发起点感到不解，或许认为Batch并不是最合适的工具。

• [简短正面观点 - bonki] bonki简单表达了对该事件的赞赏，称其为"Supercool!"，但未深入阐述原因，显示出对该成就的认可和支持。

补充讨论：
- 评论中nootis的个人经历展示了Batch在某些人编程旅程中的独特地位，尽管它可能不是最现代或最适合游戏开发的工具。
- codingbot3000的质疑引出了一个讨论点，即Batch是否适合作为游戏开发的起点，这可能涉及对编程语言选择和学习路径的更广泛讨论。
- 整体来看，评论互动较为简短，但展示了不同用户对同一事件的多样化看法，尤其是情感上的共鸣和质疑之间的张力。

About
This is an old-school DDA raycaster made in Windows Batch. This project is notable for its functionality despite Batch's lack of floating point arithmetic or built-in trigonometric functions.
Per Batch's limitations, frames take roughly 1.5 seconds to generate and movement is done via console-inputs (
set /p
).

.

back to top

Getting started
Prerequisites
Designed exclusively for Windows. Functionality within Linux/macOS virtual environments may vary (e.g.
wine
).
Installation
Clone/download the repo
git clone https://github.com/nTh0rn/batch-raycaster.git
(
back to top
)
Usage
Modify
map.txt
to contain the map of your choice. By default, the character '
·
' middle-dot,
U+00B7
, denotes empty cells.
Double click
raycaster.bat
or execute from Command Prompt.

3.1
w
=north,
a
=west,
s
=south,
d
=east
3.2
z #
=aim left,
x #
=aim right, where
#
is the number of degrees to turn.

Run
optimized/raycaster_optimized.bat
instead of
raycaster.bat
for greatly increased performance at the cost of unreadable code.

data.title: The Precise Language of Good Management
data.author: thisismytest
data.article_summary:
文章强调了管理者使用精确语言的重要性，指出许多管理者常因紧张、懒惰或缺乏经验而说话模糊，导致误解和困惑。文章提供了几个常见的不精确语言例子及改进建议：

1. **绩效反馈**：当员工问及表现时，管理者应避免即兴给出不具体反馈，如"总体不错，但沟通需改善"，而应表示需要时间准备更详尽的回答。
   
2. **绩效评估**：避免使用模糊、夸赞的语言，如"非常出色"，应具体描述行为，如"在需求变更中表现出坚持"。

3. **任务分配**：当被问及团队是否能完成任务时，避免简单回答"可以"或"不行"，应收集更多信息后给出具体答复，说明可能需要做出的权衡。

文章建议管理者应学会使用精确语言，并通过书面记录来促进这种习惯，以确保沟通清晰、有效。附录中还提供了更多关于晋升、PIP（绩效改进计划）、招聘和目标设定时的具体语言示例。

06 Apr 2025
•
management
As a manager, your words are your bond
In the squishy realm of managing humans, the specific things you say have specific outcomes.
Unfortunately, most managers are very bad at speaking precisely. Speaking precisely, especially about long-term, uncertain things, is not something many people do by nature.
To compound issues, there are a variety of factors that drive managers to speak non-specifically and say the wrong thing. These include things like:
Nervousness or laziness
Lack of experience
Not wanting to disappoint people
Not wanting to seem like you don’t have the answer
Let’s explore some common examples of imprecise language and how to fix them.
Common Examples
How Am I Doing?
The most common example of imprecise language is when someone asks you in a 1:1 “how am I doing?” Very few managers are ready to answer this question well on the spot. But managers answer the question anyway and often say things like:
“Oh you’re doing well, communication could improve a bit but overall you’re doing well.”
Well, what often happens is that the performance round happens and the person gets below expectations.
“I thought I was doing well?”
Yes, you did say that. You didn’t say that the communication piece is actually a major factor in their performance that is causing regular friction in the team.
The right answer in this situation is almost always to say that you need some time to gather your thoughts and will come to the next 1:1 with a more considered answer. By default this should be your answer any time anyone asks you how they’re doing, because unless you hold a ton of information in your head at all times and have regularly reviewed it for an accurate synthesis of their performance, there’s no way you can answer that question specifically, or well.
Performance Assessments
I mentioned this topic in our article on writing performance reviews. It’s extremely common for managers to use vague and overly flowery language in performance reviews.
Imagine you’re a junior engineer and you get a review that says:
“Angela is a great engineer and always up for a challenge.”
Problems:
If Angela is a junior engineer and is already “great”, what does growth look like? Have they already peaked?
Feedback is to either tell someone what to change or what to keep doing. “Great engineer” does none of that.
People change. You’re describing them as having invariant properties vs. describing things they’ve done. This makes it harder for people to process feedback that’s counter to these claims in the future.
So, be very specific in what you’re calling out, and give feedback around actions, not attributes. Good examples:
“Angela showed impressive persistence in delivering her feature through several requirements changes”
“Angela is a detail-oriented code reviewer, much to the benefit of our team”
Can You Do This?
Another common example of unspecific language happens when your boss asks you if your team can do something. There’s two common, bad answers that people habitually use:
Yes, we can (The refrain of yes men everywhere)
No we can’t, we have too much to do, we’d have to make tradeoffs that would collapse the company (The refrain of people who are afraid of their team)
The problem is that neither of these answers are specific or true. The right answer here is to gather more information and circle back. But if there are meaningful tradeoffs, the right answer is always:
“We probably can but let me draw out the implications of taking on this work so we can align on priorities.”
Summary
The point here is that specific language really matters. “Good” is not the same as “persistent”. “Soon” is not the same thing as “6 months.”
One of the reasons why writing things down all the time is so useful is that it forces people into more measured, specific language. If you’re a manager, using measured and specific language needs to be a skill you learn ASAP.
Appendix: More Examples
Here’s a bunch of examples where people often use vague language when they shouldn’t:
Promotions
Don’t: “I think a promotion soon is looking good.”
Do: “We have two promotion cycles in the next 12 months. I think the one in 3 months is less likely and the one in 9 months is about 80% there. Let’s discuss why I’m thinking about those probabilities and we can make sure you feel that’s fair.”
PIPs
Don’t: “Hey these last two weeks have been great.”
Do: “These last two weeks have been at the level of output we determined was necessary for you to succeed in this PIP. You’ll have to keep this up for the remainder to pass.”
Hiring
Don’t: “Yeah you can basically choose your team once you’re in.”
Do: “We have three teams that have open roles right now. One of them you aren’t a fit for based on your background, so realistically that leaves two and of those two the X team seems like a better fit, so if you wouldn’t want to join that team, let’s talk”
Goals
Don’t: “That’ll get done next quarter.”
Do: “Our target date for that is March 1st.”

2. **绩效评估**：避免使用模糊、夸赞的语言，如"非常出色"，应具体描述行为，如"在需求变更中表现出坚持"。

3. **任务分配**：当被问及团队是否能完成任务时，避免简单回答"可以"或"不行"，应收集更多信息后给出具体答复，说明可能需要做出的权衡。

文章建议管理者应学会使用精确语言，并通过书面记录来促进这种习惯，以确保沟通清晰、有效。附录中还提供了更多关于晋升、PIP（绩效改进计划）、招聘和目标设定时的具体语言示例。

data.title: Dead Stars Don’t Radiate
data.author: thechao
data.article_summary: 文章主要讨论了Michael F. Wondrak等三人声称任何大质量物体，即使不是黑洞，也会发出霍金辐射，并预言这将导致宇宙更早消亡。他们认为，死去的冷恒星会通过霍金辐射缓慢失去质量并最终消失，但这违反了重子数守恒定律。该主张在物理学界几乎没有引起影响，因为专家们认为这是错误的。他们的研究使用了粗略的近似方法，得出了错误结论。实际上，自1975年以来，专家们已知静态质量的引力场不会产生粒子-反粒子对。多篇评论文章和早期研究（如Abhay Ashtekar和Anne Magnon的工作）都表明，静态时空中的真空是稳定的。尽管媒体大肆宣传，但这些研究结果并未获得学术界的认可，提醒读者不应轻信新闻稿的宣传。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对宇宙学和大尺度物理理论的探讨，包括霍金辐射、引力辐射、学术发表问题以及科学传播中的问题。

不同观点：
• [chrz] 认为目前的大理论缺少对宇宙中某些未解现象的解释，未来几十亿年的理论可能遗漏了一些关键因素。
• [gruturo] 质疑在没有超过光速的重力井的情况下，霍金辐射如何发生，并指出如果虚拟粒子-反粒子对都存活下来并迅速消失，那么这一场景下霍金辐射无法发生。
• [qnleigh] 提问为何大质量物体不辐射引力波，并提到Unruh效应，询问其是否与霍金辐射有关联。
• [A_D_E_P_T] 认为某篇论文是无意义的，指出预印本服务器上发表的一些内容往往无法通过同行评审，并举例两年前的韩国“超导体”事件来说明媒体在报道科学新闻时应更加谨慎。
• [nimish] 认为学术知识被割裂在各个孤岛中，不同领域之间的知识共享不足，这阻碍了整体知识的进步，并指出这不是个别研究者的愚蠢所致，而是学术体系的问题。

补充讨论：
• [cvoss] 认为量子场论在弯曲时空中不守恒是已知的，尤其是通过霍金辐射理论，并批评某篇博客文章中情绪化的语言不适合科学说服。
• [layer8] 对Ashtekar和Magnon在其1975年论文中假设时空是全局双曲的提出疑问，认为现代假设应是时空是全局平坦的。
• [tbrownaw] 提到有人试图通过简化计算来制造永动机的现象，暗示对科学理论的误用。
• [w10-1] 讨论科学中的虚假信息问题，指出科学界缺乏有效的防御机制，且因科学家之间的争辩看起来像政治斗争，导致科学失去公信力。
• [BlueTemplar] 引用马克·吐温的名言（尽管实际上可能是误传）来说明谎言传播速度快于真相，并提供了一个相关引用的调查链接。
• [globnomulous] 批评不从事某领域研究的人仅凭找到的“研究”就发表意见，认为不了解研究方法的人无法正确评估研究质量。
• [cubefox] 提到之前在Hacker News上关于宇宙可能在10^78年后衰变的讨论。
• [lproven] 引用研究者Eskil Simonsson的观点，指出“死星仍在燃烧”。
• [JohnMakin] 开玩笑地表示这对Boltzmann大脑来说是个好消息。
• [m3kw9] 对预测几万亿年之后的事件表示怀疑，认为物理学无法证明如此遥远的未来事件。

争议焦点：
1. 霍金辐射在特定情况下的发生机制以及虚拟粒子对的命运。
2. 学术论文的质量和媒体在报道科学发现时的责任。
3. 知识孤岛问题是否阻碍了科学进步。
4. 科学公信力因内部争辩而受损的问题。

44015872.article_content:
Azimuth
Home
About
Dead Stars Don’t Radiate
Three guys claim that any heavy chunk of matter emits Hawking radiation, even if it’s not a black hole:
• Michael F. Wondrak, Walter D. van Suijlekom and Heino Falcke,
Gravitational pair production and black hole evaporation
,
Phys. Rev. Lett.
130
(2023), 221502.
Now they’re getting more publicity by claiming this will make the universe fizzle out sooner than expected.
They’re claiming
, for example, that a dead, cold star will emit Hawking radiation, and thus slowly lose mass and eventually disappear!
They admit that this would violate baryon conservation: after all, the protons and neutrons in the star would have to go away somehow!  They admit they don’t know how this would happen.  They just say that the gravitational field of the star will create particle-antiparticle pairs that will slowly radiate away, forcing the dead star to lose mass
somehow
to conserve energy.
If experts thought this had even a chance of being true, it would be the biggest thing since sliced bread—at least in the field of quantum gravity.  Everyone would be writing papers about it, because if true it would be revolutionary.   It would overturn calculations by experts which say that a stationary chunk of matter doesn’t emit Hawking radiation.  It would also mean that quantum field theory in curved spacetime can only be consistent if baryon number fails to be conserved!  This would be utterly shocking.
But in fact, these new papers have had almost zero effect on physics.  There’s a short rebuttal, here:
• Antonio Ferreiro José Navarro-Salas and Silvia Pla,
Comment on “Gravitational pair production and black hole evaporation”
,
Phys. Rev. Lett.
133
(2024), 229001.
It explains that these guys used a crude approximation that gives wrong results even in a simpler problem.   Similar points are made here:
• E. T. Akhmedov, D. V. Diakonov and C. Schubert,
Complex effective actions and gravitational pair creation
,
Phys. Rev. D.
110
, 105011.
Unfortunately, it seems the real experts on quantum field theory in curved spacetime have not come out and mentioned the
correct
way to think about this issue, which has been known at least since 1975.  To them—or maybe I should dare to say “us”—it’s just
well known
that the gravitational field of a static mass does not cause the creation of particle-antiparticle pairs.
Of course, the referees should have rejected Wondrak, van Suijlekom and Falcke’s papers.  But apparently none of those referees were experts on the subject at hand.  So you can’t trust a paper just because it appears in a supposedly reputable physics journal.  You have to actually understand the subject and assess the paper yourself, or talk to some experts you trust.
If I were a science journalist writing an article about a supposedly shocking development like this, I would email some experts and check to see if it’s for real.  But plenty of science journalists don’t bother with that anymore: they just believe the press releases.  So now we’re being bombarded with lazy articles like these:
•
Universe will die “much sooner than expected,” new research says
,
CBS News
, May 13, 2025.
• Sharmila Kuthunur,
Scientists calculate when the universe will end—it’s sooner than expected
,
Space.com
, 15 May 2025.
• Jamie Carter,
The universe will end sooner than thought, scientists say
,
Forbes
, 16 May 2025.
The list goes on; these are just three.   There’s no way what I say can have much effect against such a flood of misinformation.  As Mark Twain said, “A lie can travel around the world and back again while the truth is lacing up its boots.”  Actually he probably didn’t say that—but everyone keeps saying he did, illustrating the point perfectly.
Still, there might be a few people who both care and don’t already know this stuff.  Instead of trying to give a mini-course here, let me simply point to an explanation of how things really work:
• Abhay Ashtekar and Anne Magnon,
Quantum fields in curved space-times
,
Proceedings of the Royal Society
,
346
(1975), 375–394.
It’s technical, so it’s not easy reading if you haven’t studied quantum field theory and general relativity, but that’s unavoidable.  It shows that in a static spacetime there is a well-defined concept of ‘vacuum’, and the vacuum is stable.  Jorge Pullin pointed out the key sentence for present purposes:
Thus, if the underlying space-time admits a everywhere time-like Killing field, the vacuum state is indeed stable and phenomena such as the spontaneous creation of particles do not occur.
This condition of having an “everywhere time-like Killing field” says that a spacetime has time translation symmetry.  Ashtekar and Magnon also assume that spacetime is globally hyperbolic and that the wave equation for a massive spin-zero particle has a smooth solution given smooth initial data.  All this lets us define a concept of energy for solutions of this equation.  It also lets us split solutions into positive-frequency solutions, which correspond

data.title: Coding without a laptop: Two weeks with AR glasses and Linux on Android
data.author: mikenew
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者如何在手机上运行完整的Linux桌面环境，而无需使用虚拟机或替换操作系统。通过chroot容器，作者成功运行了如i3窗口管理器、Firefox浏览器等原生arm64程序。作者为了实现无需携带笔记本电脑的旅行工作模式，搭配了折叠键盘和AR眼镜，利用手机的DisplayPort功能驱动显示。整套设备包括二手的Pixel 8 Pro手机、Xreal Air 2 Pro AR眼镜和折叠键盘，总成本为636美元。

这套设置让作者可以在户外、咖啡店、飞机上等各种场所工作，具有便携性和自由度。尽管搭建Linux环境有一定难度，但最终实现了如Neovim编程、Flutter调试等开发功能。作者认为，这种设置带来了笔记本电脑无法提供的便携和自由感，特别适合户外工作。不过，过程中也遇到了一些困难和细节问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AR眼镜和相关技术在实际应用中的可行性、舒适性及未来发展

不同观点：
• **Johnh-hn**：作为一位视力受损用户，他希望找到一种能够替代传统显示器、减少身体不适的解决方案。他提到目前通过靠近屏幕勉强使用显示器，但长期的姿势导致背部和颈部问题。他希望通过AR眼镜完全摆脱显示器，但对AR技术了解不多，不确定是否适合自己。

• **Titzer**：分享了自己使用AR眼镜的实际体验。他喜欢这些眼镜，但指出它们存在过热问题，特别是在阳光下使用时。他还提到这些眼镜实际上并不是真正的增强现实设备，只是提供了一个浮动屏幕，并且缺乏运动追踪功能。此外，桌面支持有限，3D模式下的超宽显示也让常规笔记本使用变得困难。

• **Transpute**：讨论了在Android设备上运行Linux的各种方法，并提到即将推出的Android 2025中的Linux终端功能，该功能旨在将Linux应用程序引入Android，但不提供新的桌面环境。他希望未来Android和iOS的竞争能推动智能眼镜的发展。

• **TuringNYC**：强调了开发专用设备时，提供良好开发者体验和模拟器支持的重要性。他以Google Glass为例，指出缺乏模拟器支持是其开发过程中的一大失误，导致开发者需要不断在实际硬件上测试，增加了开发难度和不适。

• **D_burfoot**：认为计算机界面设计即将迎来一场革命，期望未来能够摆脱桌面束缚，利用语音识别、AR/VR、LLMs等新技术实现更自由的工作方式。

• **Stratoscope**：不使用AR眼镜，但分享了一款他喜欢的手机用便携键盘（iClever BK05），并描述了其良好的使用体验和便携性。他指出该键盘适合在移动环境中使用，并且不会影响打字体验。

• **Hansmayer**：对在户外环境（如公园或长椅）中工作的可行性表示怀疑，认为即使有AR眼镜，也难以在这种环境中保持高效生产力。

• **Two_handfuls**：提到在VR头戴设备上进行游戏开发的例子，认为这些非传统计算设备正变得越来越有用，尽管与主讨论点不直接相关，但展示了AR/VR设备的潜力。

• **Montebicyclelo**：提到在手机上进行root操作的困难和风险，特别是由于Google引入了反回滚 bootloader 导致的一些设备在尝试root时变砖的问题。

• **Resonious**：曾尝试使用手机加眼镜加外接键盘的组合，但最终还是回归笔记本电脑。他认为笔记本电脑的即开即用特性更适合他的需求，而手机加眼镜组合需要太多准备步骤。

• **Npilk**：认为Xreal眼镜在短期内将成为AR/VR领域的赢家，因为它提供了一种便携的个人屏幕体验，能够将手机内容以更大、更私密的形式呈现，而不试图建立全新的生态系统。

• **Zmmmmm**：对AR眼镜长期停留在1080p分辨率表示怀疑，认为这是技术上的停滞。他希望看到更高的分辨率，如2560x1600，否则对这种设备持怀疑态度。

• **Ireadmevs**：推荐使用机械键盘，并分享了自建36键便携键盘的经验，认为这种键盘不仅便携而且功能强大，可以映射键位来控制鼠标等操作。

• **Tomaskafka**：对Termux的功能表示惊叹，认为这种技术可以让他在度假时无需携带昂贵的MacBook，仅通过iPad和键盘完成一些紧急修复工作。

• **Inatreecrown2**：担心长时间使用AR眼镜会对眼睛造成损害，特别是长时间聚焦在短距离的屏幕上。他希望有使用经验的人能分享这方面的看法。

补充讨论：
• AR眼镜的实际应用和开发者体验问题
• 不同用户对便携设备和键盘的偏好
• 对未来技术发展的期待和疑虑
• 技术实现中的具体问题，如过热、分辨率限制和root风险

43985513.article_content:
I recently learned something that blew my mind;
you can run a full desktop Linux environment on your phone.
Not some clunky virtual machine
and not an outright OS replacement like Ubuntu Touch or postmarketOS.
Just native arm64 binaries running inside
a little chroot container on Android. Check it out:
i3, picom, polybar, firefox, and htop
That's a graphical environment via X11 with real window management and compositing,
Firefox comfortably playing YouTube (including working audio),
and a status bar with system stats.
It launches in less than a second and feels snappy.
Ignoring the details of getting this to work for the moment,
the obvious response is "okay yeah that's neat but like,
why
".
And fair enough. It's novel, but surely not useful.
Thing is, I had a 2 week trip coming up where I'd need to work,
and I got a little obsessed with the idea
that I could somehow leave my laptop at home and
just use my phone
.
So what if we add a folding keyboard and some AR glasses?
Here's a CRDT-based ebook/audiobook reader I've been working on,
running a desktop Linux app and connected to the Flutter debugger.
What's kind of amazing here is that both the glasses and the keyboard
fit comfortably in my pockets.
And I'm already carrying the phone, so it's not that much extra.
The Hardware
​
Keyboard:
There's plenty of little folding bluetooth keyboards on the market,
and I only had to go through 5 of them before I
found one
that was tolerable.
I tried some with trackpads, but they were either too big
or the keys were squeezed together to make it fit.
The Termux
:X11
app that displays the graphical environment
is able to function as a trackpad to move a mouse pointer around,
and that turned out to be good enough for mouse input.
I'm very keyboard-centric anyway,
so I'd often go for a while without needing to touch it.
The Glasses:
Believe it or not, "augmented reality" glasses are kinda good now.
The AR part is almost entirely a misnomer; they're just tiny little OLED displays
strapped to your face attached to bird bath optics.
I was able to get a lightly used pair of
Xreal Air 2 Pros
off of ebay that would show me a 1080p display
with a 46° field of view.
Some of the newer ones can do large virtual displays rather than the
pinned-to-your-head image that mine have,
but I'm pretty skeptical of that setup,
at least until the resolution and field of view improve.
The Phone:
I unfortunately had to upgrade my phone,
because to drive the glasses you need to have DisplayPort Alt mode.
My very cheap, very crappy old phone did not.
The 8 series seems to be the first Pixel phone where Google decided to be marginally less evil
and not lock out the DP Alt Mode feature in software (forcing people to buy Chromecasts? IDK),
so I bought a used
Pixel 8 Pro
on ebay.
So the whole setup:
Used Pixel 8 Pro $350
Used Xreal Air 2 Pro - $260
Samers Foldable Keyboard $18
Total cost: $636. Although I'm not sure the $350 for the phone should count,
because I really did need a new one.
After a few afternoons experimenting,
I felt like I could
probably
function with only this setup for the two weeks.
I figured the full commit would keep me from reverting back to a PC
when I hit a wall and got frustrated or bored.
The Result
​
So after using this on an airplane, in coffee shops, at various family member's houses,
in parks, and even sitting in the car, I think I have some answers for
"why would you use this when laptops exist and are excellent".
It really does fit into your pockets. No bag, nothing to carry.
I can use it outdoors in bright sunlight. I wrote most of this blog post sitting at a picnic table in a park.
Screen glare and brightness is not an issue.
I can fit into tight spaces. This setup was infinitely more comfortable than a laptop when on a plane.
Some coffee shops also have narrow bars that are too small for a laptop, but not for this.
The phone has a cellular connection, so I'm not tied to wifi.
In other words, there's a sense of freedom that you do not get with a laptop.
And I can be
outdoors
.
One of the things I've grown tired of as software dev
is feeling like I'm stuck inside all the time in front of a screen.
With this I can walk to a coffee shop and work for an hour or two,
then get up and walk to a park for another hour of work.
There really is this amazing sense of freedom.
That said, there were plenty of pain points and nuances to the whole thing.
So here's my experience:
The Linux Environment
​
Linux-on-Android was
eventually
great,
but I don't want to gloss over the fact that it was a pain in the ass to figure out.
My definition of "sufficiently capable" was Neovim + functioning langauge servers
(Nim, Python, Dart, JS), Node, and Flutter
(compiling to both desktop and web apps that could be run and debugged).

43985513.article_summary:
本文介绍了作者如何在手机上运行完整的Linux桌面环境，而无需使用虚拟机或替换操作系统。通过chroot容器，作者成功运行了如i3窗口管理器、Firefox浏览器等原生arm64程序。作者为了实现无需携带笔记本电脑的旅行工作模式，搭配了折叠键盘和AR眼镜，利用手机的DisplayPort功能驱动显示。整套设备包括二手的Pixel 8 Pro手机、Xreal Air 2 Pro AR眼镜和折叠键盘，总成本为636美元。

这套设置让作者可以在户外、咖啡店、飞机上等各种场所工作，具有便携性和自由度。尽管搭建Linux环境有一定难度，但最终实现了如Neovim编程、Flutter调试等开发功能。作者认为，这种设置带来了笔记本电脑无法提供的便携和自由感，特别适合户外工作。不过，过程中也遇到了一些困难和细节问题。

不同观点：
• **Johnh-hn**：作为一位视力受损用户，他希望找到一种能够替代传统显示器、减少身体不适的解决方案。他提到目前通过靠近屏幕勉强使用显示器，但长期的姿势导致背部和颈部问题。他希望通过AR眼镜完全摆脱显示器，但对AR技术了解不多，不确定是否适合自己。

• **Titzer**：分享了自己使用AR眼镜的实际体验。他喜欢这些眼镜，但指出它们存在过热问题，特别是在阳光下使用时。他还提到这些眼镜实际上并不是真正的增强现实设备，只是提供了一个浮动屏幕，并且缺乏运动追踪功能。此外，桌面支持有限，3D模式下的超宽显示也让常规笔记本使用变得困难。

• **Transpute**：讨论了在Android设备上运行Linux的各种方法，并提到即将推出的Android 2025中的Linux终端功能，该功能旨在将Linux应用程序引入Android，但不提供新的桌面环境。他希望未来Android和iOS的竞争能推动智能眼镜的发展。

• **TuringNYC**：强调了开发专用设备时，提供良好开发者体验和模拟器支持的重要性。他以Google Glass为例，指出缺乏模拟器支持是其开发过程中的一大失误，导致开发者需要不断在实际硬件上测试，增加了开发难度和不适。

• **D_burfoot**：认为计算机界面设计即将迎来一场革命，期望未来能够摆脱桌面束缚，利用语音识别、AR/VR、LLMs等新技术实现更自由的工作方式。

• **Stratoscope**：不使用AR眼镜，但分享了一款他喜欢的手机用便携键盘（iClever BK05），并描述了其良好的使用体验和便携性。他指出该键盘适合在移动环境中使用，并且不会影响打字体验。

• **Hansmayer**：对在户外环境（如公园或长椅）中工作的可行性表示怀疑，认为即使有AR眼镜，也难以在这种环境中保持高效生产力。

• **Two_handfuls**：提到在VR头戴设备上进行游戏开发的例子，认为这些非传统计算设备正变得越来越有用，尽管与主讨论点不直接相关，但展示了AR/VR设备的潜力。

• **Montebicyclelo**：提到在手机上进行root操作的困难和风险，特别是由于Google引入了反回滚 bootloader 导致的一些设备在尝试root时变砖的问题。

• **Resonious**：曾尝试使用手机加眼镜加外接键盘的组合，但最终还是回归笔记本电脑。他认为笔记本电脑的即开即用特性更适合他的需求，而手机加眼镜组合需要太多准备步骤。

• **Npilk**：认为Xreal眼镜在短期内将成为AR/VR领域的赢家，因为它提供了一种便携的个人屏幕体验，能够将手机内容以更大、更私密的形式呈现，而不试图建立全新的生态系统。

• **Zmmmmm**：对AR眼镜长期停留在1080p分辨率表示怀疑，认为这是技术上的停滞。他希望看到更高的分辨率，如2560x1600，否则对这种设备持怀疑态度。

• **Ireadmevs**：推荐使用机械键盘，并分享了自建36键便携键盘的经验，认为这种键盘不仅便携而且功能强大，可以映射键位来控制鼠标等操作。

• **Tomaskafka**：对Termux的功能表示惊叹，认为这种技术可以让他在度假时无需携带昂贵的MacBook，仅通过iPad和键盘完成一些紧急修复工作。

• **Inatreecrown2**：担心长时间使用AR眼镜会对眼睛造成损害，特别是长时间聚焦在短距离的屏幕上。他希望有使用经验的人能分享这方面的看法。

data.author: p-s-v
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了刀具钢材的性能对比，包括耐腐蚀性、韧性、刃口保持性和易 sharpening 性，评分范围为1-10。用户可以选择最多5种钢材进行比较。文章列出了多组钢材的对比分析图表，如1095与5160、154CM与S30V、20CV与M390等。对比内容涵盖各种钢材在不同性能指标下的表现，帮助用户选择适合需求的刀具钢材。文章提供了超过150种钢材的详细对比，其中147种附有图表。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：刀具钢材性能的数据来源、种类、性能平衡及工具改进建议

不同观点：
• [数据来源质疑] **kurthr** 和 **ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7** 对数据来源提出疑问。**kurthr** 希望了解钢材硬度等数据是否来自可信的数据库或自行测量，并指出热处理对刀具性能的影响被忽视。**ZYbCRq22HbJ2y7** 甚至怀疑数据是否由大型语言模型生成，并对数据的准确性提出质疑。

• [请求添加常用钢材] **LooseMarmoset** 建议加入 80CRV、1084、1075 等常用钢材，并提到 440 钢有多个等级。他还指出锰含量和钢材硬化深度对刀具性能的影响。**abcd_f** 则询问是否计划加入日本钢材。**williadc** 特别提到 Sandvik 14c28n 作为预算刀具的常用钢材。

• [工具使用和改进建议] **reconnecting** 对如何分析钢材类型表示好奇，并分享了个人使用历史刀具的经验。**hunter-gatherer** 对工具表示赞赏，但提到自己使用的 White River 刀具（CPM Magnacut）尚未经过长时间测试。**out-of-ideas** 建议在图表中保持颜色一致，以提高可读性。**bberenberg** 希望看到钢材按多边形面积排名的列表。

• [性能平衡讨论] **keisborg** 对刀具钢材是否能在刃口保持性、易磨性和韧性之间取得良好平衡表示怀疑，并希望看到钢材性能的实例分析。

补充讨论：
• [其他数据库对比] **eichin** 提到另一个刀具数据库，并指出该数据库虽然有大量数值测试结果数据，但钢材仅以“市场名称”显示。他提供了该数据库的原始数据链接，供进一步比较。

• [陶瓷刀具讨论] **adamgordonbell** 提到陶瓷刀具的优缺点，指出其超锐利但易碎的特点，与其他讨论的钢材形成对比。

争议焦点：
• 数据的可信度和来源是争议的核心，部分用户对数据的准确性和来源提出质疑，希望看到更透明和详细的数据支持。

data.title: Catalog of Novel Operating Systems
data.author: prathyvsh
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了一个由prathyvsh创建的名为"os-catalog"的项目，该项目旨在收录新颖的操作系统。文章回顾了过去一些独特的操作系统，如AmigaOS、BeOS和Plan9等，并指出在笔记应用热潮之后，许多人开始大胆地构建新的操作系统。文章详细列举了多个现代实验性操作系统，包括UXN、Playbit、Folk.computer、Nette.io、Interim、Mezzano、ChrysalLisp、RayvnOS、RedoxOS、DesktopNeo、MercuryOS和WormOS，并提供了相关文档和链接。项目作者对每个操作系统进行了简要描述，强调了它们的创新点和独特之处，展示了当前操作系统开发的多样性和创造力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：操作系统的定义与创新方向

不同观点：
• gnramires认为不应重新开发完整的操作系统，而应专注于“操作环境”（Operating Environment, OE），如Emacs、浏览器或pico-8等，通过复用底层主机操作系统功能来提供新的用户界面和体验。他指出，开发低级别系统如文件系统和设备驱动非常困难，且现有系统如Linux已经支持大量设备。他还提到，操作系统的用户界面应注重用户体验，不应对用户操作造成障碍，且可以自动化任务。

• MomsAVoxell从怀旧和复古计算的角度，提到过去使用过的独特系统（如Wang Imaging System），并表示重温这些高概念的计算环境是一种乐趣。他拥有大量复古计算设备，并乐于重新安装和使用这些系统。

• maxlin建议将SerenityOS纳入讨论，认为它是真正从头构建的常见操作系统，具有公开开发的特点，且其代码库相对易于理解。

• alphazard指出seL4和Helios的重要性，强调适当的沙盒机制的缺乏以及由此导致的问题，如Linux容器和虚拟机的使用。他还提到由于单片内核的开发摩擦导致文件系统和网络的停滞。

• Lerc关注多处理器系统的支持，询问是否有从设计之初就为大量处理器优化的操作系统。

• mindcrime开玩笑地表示期待看到Novell操作系统的目录，暗示对讨论内容的不同期望。

• xattt指出每个条目都代表了开发者的努力，强调人类投入的重要性。

• serhack_希望看到超越WIMP（窗口、图标、菜单、指针）界面的操作系统示例。

• jeffbee认为标题应为“UI演示目录”，指出讨论内容更偏向于用户界面而非操作系统本身，并提到过去如Desktop Neo的演示。

• rubitxxx3认为列表可以更长，提到计算机科学学生和爱好者常进行此类开发，质疑内容格式是否过于冗长。

• diego_moita批评人们通常只关注图形用户界面和桌面管理器等表层内容，忽视了如电子阅读器、路由器、智能手表等专用设备的操作系统创新。

补充讨论：
• justanothersys提到自己创建的基于网页的美学计算机项目，提供了一种不同的操作系统体验。
• zhainya提到TempleOS，这是一个独特的操作系统，值得讨论。
• gitroom表达了对旧或怪异操作系统内容的喜爱，激发个人重新探索旧设备。

争议焦点：
• 操作系统与操作环境的区别及其实际应用价值。
• 操作系统开发中低级别技术与用户界面创新的优先级。
• 专用设备操作系统与通用操作系统的发展方向。

Novel Operating Systems Catalog
Catalogue of novel operating systems
Somewhere after the fall in popularity of note-taking apps, perhaps recognizing that just note-taking is not enough and the deafening hype of LLMs, there was a sweet period of lull when a lot of people started boldly building new operating systems. This is a catalogue of such operating systems that I have come across. In the past, before the commercialization of computers, we had a plethora of operating systems with unique languages to interact with computers, like AmigaOS, Symbolics, SunOS, MULTICS, Burroughs, Meneut, BeOS PARC, Star, Oberon, Plan9, NeXTSTEP, OS/2, PL/8, Inferno, QNX, RISCOS etc. This spirit can only be glimpsed in pockets, and kudos to all those who keep the fire alive!
A thread on it
here
.
UXN
Perhaps the best one to start off this catalog is the UXN/Varvara personal computing stack of
100 Rabbits
. Such a great couple with such a radical vision!
They have documented their rationale in these two documents:
Tools Ecosystem
Weathering Software Winter
Documents related to UXN can be obtained here:
https://github.com/hundredrabbits/awesome-uxn?tab=readme-ov-file
Playbit
Daring effort from
Rasmus Andersson
and team to reinvent the computer stack.
And alpha version available
here
.
Folk.computer
Folk computer by Omar Rizwan and Andreas Cuérvo is a research project centered around building physical computing interfaces. It shares its roots from Bret Victor’s
Dynamicland
.
Nette.io
Nette.io by
Pawel Ceranka
positions itself as a research OS for the web.
Interim
Something about Lisp draws people into construct OSes from ground up. Perhaps it is the simplicity of the language that acts as the foundation. Here‘s Interim, one of our favourite minimal OSes constructed with Lisp.
Mezzano
An OS written in CommonLisp
ChrysalLisp
ChrysaLisp is amulti-threaded, multi-core, multi-user parallel OS with features such as a GUI, terminal, OO Assembler, class libraries, C-Script compiler, Lisp interpreter, debugger, profiler, vector font engine, and more.

data.author: giuliomagnifico
data.article_summary: 科学家首次通过延时摄影捕捉到了心脏形成的瞬间。利用先进的光片显微技术，研究团队观察到小鼠胚胎中的心脏细胞在早期发育过程中自发组织成心脏形状。这些细胞在原肠胚形成阶段迅速出现，并遵循特定路径，形成心室和心房。通过荧光标记和每两分钟一次的拍摄，研究人员记录了细胞移动、分裂并形成原始心脏器官的过程。该研究揭示了心脏发育的早期调控机制，挑战了现有模型，并为理解和治疗先天性心脏缺陷提供了新见解，可能推动再生医学中心脏组织的生长。研究结果发表在《EMBO Journal》上。

Moment a heart begins to form captured in time-lapse for the first time – video
Biology
Moment of heart’s formation captured in images for first time
Time-lapse footage reveals cardiac cells in a mouse embryo begin to organise themselves during early development
Hannah Devlin
Science correspondent
Tue 13 May 2025 10.31 EDT
Share
The moment a heart begins to form has been captured in extraordinary time-lapse images for the first time.
The footage reveals cardiac cells in a mouse embryo begin to spontaneously organise themselves into a heart-like shape early in development. Scientists say the technique could provide new insights into congenital heart defects, which affect nearly one in 100 babies.
“This is the first time we’ve been able to watch heart cells this closely, for this long, during mammalian development,” said the study’s senior author, Dr Kenzo Ivanovitch of University College London’s Great Ormond Street Institute of Child Health. “We first had to reliably grow the embryos in a dish over long periods, from a few hours to a few days, and what we found was totally unexpected.”
The footage of the developing embryos was captured using a technique called advanced light-sheet microscopy. This allowed scientists to track the embryos as they went through a developmental milestone known as gastrulation, when the embryo begins to form distinct cell lines and starts to establish the basic axes of the body.
Soon after, heart muscle cells organise themselves into a large tube that will go on to divide into sections that will eventually become the walls and chambers. In babies with heart defects, a hole can form during this process.
Using fluorescent markers, the team tagged heart muscle cells called cardiomyocytes, causing them to glow in distinct colours. Snapshots were captured every two minutes over 40 hours, showing the cells moving, dividing and forming a primitive organ. This allowed the team to see when and where the first cells that make the heart appeared in the embryo.
The researchers found that early during gastrulation (about six days into mouse embryo development), cells contributing solely to the heart emerged rapidly and behaved in highly organised ways. Rather than moving randomly, they began to follow distinct paths, whether contributing to the ventricles (the heart’s pumping chambers) or the atria (where blood enters the heart from the body and lungs).
“Our findings demonstrate that cardiac fate determination and directional cell movement may be regulated much earlier in the embryo than current models suggest,” said Ivanovitch. “This fundamentally changes our understanding of cardiac development by showing that what appears to be chaotic cell migration is actually governed by hidden patterns that ensure proper heart formation.”
The team said the insights could advance the understanding and treatment of congenital heart defects and accelerate progress in growing heart tissue in the lab for use in regenerative medicine.
The findings were published in
the EMBO Journal
.

data.title: Getting AI to write good SQL
data.author: richards
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Google Cloud中的文本到SQL技术，特别是通过Gemini模型实现自然语言到SQL的转换。该技术提高了开发人员和分析人员的工作效率，并使非技术用户也能直接与数据库交互。文章讨论了文本到SQL的应用场景，如BigQuery Studio和Cloud SQL Studio中的"Help me code"功能。然而，实际应用中仍面临挑战，包括提供业务特定上下文、理解用户意图以及处理SQL方言差异。业务特定上下文需要模型具备对数据库结构和语义的深刻理解，而用户意图的模糊性可能导致模型生成不准确的SQL。文章还指出，训练专门模型以适应所有数据库变化是不切实际的，因此需要其他方法来确保SQL的准确性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI工具（尤其是Google的Gemini和LLM大语言模型）在编程、SQL数据分析等技术工作中的应用及其影响

不同观点：
• 正面观点：一些用户（如wewewedxfgdf、levocardia、mark_l_watson）认为Google AI Studio和Gemini等AI工具在编程和数据分析任务中表现出色，带来了巨大的效率提升，甚至改变了工作方式。他们强调这些工具的快速进步，尤其是对编程和自然语言处理任务的帮助。
• 批评与质疑：另一部分用户（如CommenterPerson、hakanito、AdrianB1、pcblues）则对AI工具持怀疑态度，认为它们的“智能”被过度炒作，存在诸如“幻觉”（提供不存在的方法或错误信息）等问题，尤其是在处理SQL查询和复杂业务逻辑时。他们强调仍然需要专家进行验证，AI可能带来更大的风险和不确定性。
• 社会影响担忧：mykowebhn等用户担心AI工具的进步会导致软件工程师薪资和职业前景的下滑，进而影响社会的财富分配和职业选择。

补充讨论：
• 技术实现与使用方法：mritchie712和rectang等用户讨论了如何通过语义层等技术手段来提高AI工具的使用效果，并指出AI在提供思路而非直接生成代码时的价值。
• 争议焦点：AI工具是否真的能够提高工作效率以及在实际应用中是否可靠。例如，AI生成的SQL代码是否需要人工干预、验证，以及AI是否能真正理解业务需求并提供正确的解决方案。
• 应用场景讨论：tango12和danjc等用户质疑AI工具在复杂业务分析中的实际应用价值，认为非专业人士难以判断AI生成的结果是否正确和充分。

总结：讨论围绕AI工具在技术工作中的实际效果、潜在风险及其对职业和社会的影响展开，各方观点不一，但普遍关注AI工具的可靠性和应用边界。

Databases
Getting AI to write good SQL: Text-to-SQL techniques explained
May 16, 2025
Per Jacobsson
Principal Software Engineer
Try Gemini 2.5
Our most intelligent model is now available on Vertex AI
Try now
Organizations depend on fast and accurate data-driven insights to make decisions, and SQL is at the core of how they access that data. With Gemini, Google can generate SQL directly from natural language — a.k.a. text-to-SQL. This capability increases developer and analysts’ productivity and empowers non-technical users to interact directly with the data they need.
Today, you can find text-to-SQL capabilities in many Google Cloud products:
BigQuery Studio
in the
SQL Editor
and
SQL Generation tool
, and within the
Data Canvas
SQL node
"Help me code" functionality in
Cloud SQL Studio
(
Postgres, MySQL and SQLServer),
AlloyDB Studio
and
Cloud Spanner Studio
AlloyDB AI
with its direct natural language interface to the database, currently available as a public preview
Through
Vertex AI
, which lets you access the Gemini models that are the basis for these products directly
Recently, powerful large language models (LLMs) like Gemini, with their abilities to reason and synthesize, have driven remarkable advancements in the field of text-to-SQL. In this blog post, the first entry in a series, we explore the technical internals of Google Cloud's text-to-SQL agents. We will cover state-of-the-art approaches to context building and table retrieval, how to do effective evaluation of text-to-SQL quality with LLM-as-a-judge techniques, the best approaches to LLM prompting and post-processing, and how we approach techniques that allows the system to offer virtually certified correct answers.
The ‘Help me code’ feature in Cloud SQL Studio generates SQL from a text prompt
The challenges of text-to-SQL technology
Current state-of-the-art LLMs like Gemini 2.5 have reasoning capabilities that make them good at translating complex questions posed in natural language to functioning SQL, complete with joins, filters, aggregations and other difficult concepts.
To see this in action you can do a simple test in
Vertex AI Studio
. Given the prompt
"I have a database schema that contains products and orders. Write a SQL query that shows the number of orders for shoes"
, Gemini produces SQL for a hypothetical schema:
Loading...
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS NumberOfShoeOrders FROM orders o JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id WHERE p.product_name LIKE '%shoe%'.
Great, this is a good looking query. But what happens when you move beyond this trivial example, and use Gemini for text-to-SQL against a real world database and on real-world user questions? It turns out that the problem is more difficult. The model needs to be complemented with methods to:
provide business-specific context
understand user intent
manage differences in SQL dialects
Let’s take a look at each of these challenges.
Problem #1: Provide business-specific context
Just like data analysts or engineers, LLMs need significant amounts of knowledge or "context" to generate accurate SQL. The context can be both explicit (what does the schema look like, what are the relevant columns, and what does the data itself look like?) or more implicit (what is the precise semantic meaning of a piece of data? what does it mean for the specific business case?).
Specialized model training, or fine tuning, is typically not a scalable solution to this problem. Training on the shape of every database or dataset, and keeping up with schema or data changes, is both difficult and cost-prohibitive. Business knowledge and semantics are often not well documented in the first place, and difficult to turn into training data.
For example, even the best DBA in the world would not be able to write an accurate query to track shoe sales if they didn't know that
cat_id2 = 'Footwear'
in a
pcat_extension
table means that the product in question is a kind of shoe. The same is true for  LLMs.
Problem #2: Understanding user intent
Natural language is less precise than SQL. An engineer or analyst faced with an ambiguous question can detect that they need more information and go back and ask the right follow-up questions. An LLM, on the other hand, tends to try to give you an answer, and when the question is ambiguous, can be prone to hallucinating.
Example: Take a question like "What are the best-selling shoes?" Here, one obvious point of ambiguity is what "best selling" actually means in the context of the business or application — the most ordered shoes? The shoe brand that brought in the most money? Further, should the SQL count returned orders? And how many kinds of shoes do you want to see in the report? etc.
Further, different users need different kinds of answers. If the user is a technical analyst or a developer asking a vague question, giving them a reasonable, but perhaps not 100% correct SQL query is a good starting point. On the oth
44009848.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了Google Cloud中的文本到SQL技术，特别是通过Gemini模型实现自然语言到SQL的转换。该技术提高了开发人员和分析人员的工作效率，并使非技术用户也能直接与数据库交互。文章讨论了文本到SQL的应用场景，如BigQuery Studio和Cloud SQL Studio中的"Help me code"功能。然而，实际应用中仍面临挑战，包括提供业务特定上下文、理解用户意图以及处理SQL方言差异。业务特定上下文需要模型具备对数据库结构和语义的深刻理解，而用户意图的模糊性可能导致模型生成不准确的SQL。文章还指出，训练专门模型以适应所有数据库变化是不切实际的，因此需要其他方法来确保SQL的准确性。

data.title: A Simulation in C++ of Joseph Weizenbaum's 1966 Eliza
data.author: m1guelpf
data.article_summary: 这篇文章介绍了作者用C++实现的1966年Joseph Weizenbaum开发的聊天机器人ELIZA。ELIZA是一个通过脚本配置的程序，最著名的脚本是DOCTOR，它使用简单的模式匹配规则来回应用户输入，营造出理解用户的假象。作者在ELIZA源代码被发现前后分别进行了不同的改进，并与儿子用JavaScript重新创建了ELIZA。作者还为ELIZA添加了串行I/O功能，并参与证明1966年的ELIZA是图灵完备的。所有ELIZA代码都在一个文件`eliza.cpp`中，提供了在POSIX和Windows系统上构建和运行ELIZA的说明。文章还提到了一系列相关资源和项目合作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于人工智能和早期程序（如Eliza和Parry）是否能增进对智能的理解，以及这些程序是否具有真正的“智能”。

不同观点：
• [tantalor] 认为这些早期程序（如Eliza和Parry）的目的并不是为了增进对智能的理解，而是展示人们多么容易被欺骗。这实际上反映了很多关于“智能”的问题，暗示这些程序并不能真正代表智能。
• [quuxplusone] 提供了一个深入研究的资料链接，讨论了Parry和Doctor（Eliza）之间的对话，似乎对这些早期人工智能程序的历史和研究有较大兴趣，侧重于学术和历史背景。
• [throwaway81523] 提到了一个实际操作的例子，即在Emacs中通过M-x doctor命令运行Lisp版本的Eliza，更关注这些程序的实际可用性和技术实现。

Joseph Weizenbaum’s 1966 ELIZA recreated in C++
I’ve made in C++ what I think is an accurate simulation of the original ELIZA. It is a console application that takes as input the original format script file, which looks like a series of S-expressions, and then waits for the user to type a line of text before responding with a line of text of its own.
ELIZA is a chatbot—the first chatbot—written between 1964-1966 by Joseph Weizenbaum, Professor of Electrical Engineering at MIT, and part-supported by the US Department of Defence Project MAC. It is configured via a "script," the most famous of which is called DOCTOR. The script contains simple pattern matching rules that ELIZA uses to reflect back parts of the text typed in by the user. Weizenbaum's purpose was not to advance our understanding of intelligence, but to create the illusion that ELIZA understood what had been said to it in order to demonstrate how easily people can be fooled.
I made this before the ELIZA source code had been found, and wrote about it in
part 1
.
Part 2
describes changes I made after the ELIZA source code was found.
Part 3
is about the HASH function, now that too has been found.
In a
footnote
I document trying to recreate the PARRY/DOCTOR conversation from RFC439.
My son Max Hay and I recreated ELIZA in JavaScript
here
. Try it
here
.
I added
serial I/O
to run ELIZA on an ASR 33 teletype.
I helped show that 1966 CACM ELIZA is
Turing complete
.
There are several Turing machine ELIZA scripts
here
.
There is a huge collection of ELIZA-related information at Jeff Shrager's
elizagen.org
.
Along with Jeff and others I am contributing to a book about ELIZA. The website is
findingeliza.org
.
Thanks to Rupert Lane, you can now
run the original MAD ELIZA code
. (Jeff's
ELIZA Reanimated paper
.)
To build and run ELIZA
Note that the whole of ELIZA is in the one file
eliza.cpp
(unless you wish to also use the serial I/O code mentioned above).
POSIX (e.g. macOS) (I used Apple clang version 15.0.0 that came with Xcode):
clang++ -std=c++20 -pedantic -o eliza eliza.cpp
./eliza
Windows (I used Microsoft Visual Studio 2019 Community Edition Command Prompt):
cl /EHsc /W4 /std:c++20 eliza.cpp
eliza

data.title: Launch HN: Tinfoil (YC X25): Verifiable Privacy for Cloud AI
data.author: FrasiertheLion
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：隐私和安全的云计算方案及其与主流云服务商的竞争

不同观点：
• [sigmaisaletter] 认为该产品的市场规模不明，尤其是在需要最大隐私和完全不在意隐私的两类用户之间。他还提到苹果公司曾宣布过类似的“私有云计算”计划，但至今没有实际应用。他质疑该产品与苹果方案的区别和独特性。
• [Etheryte] 指出，机密计算技术是大云供应商正在或即将提供的功能，他们可以很容易地在此基础上提供大语言模型（LLM）。尽管先发优势重要，但市场可能很快会被大型云服务商吞并。
• [amanda99] 提出硬件信任根的问题，认为如果芯片制造商（如Intel）签署的代码不安全或有漏洞，整个隐私保护的目的可能会被破坏。她质疑这是否只是“合同安全”的另一种形式。
• [max_] 认为唯一能保证云计算隐私的方式是通过同态加密，并指出该方案过于依赖信任。他建议对敏感数据应在本地隔离的环境中运行模型。
• [coolcase] 担心在执行FISA令或被要求添加后门的情况下，隐私是否能得到保障。他提到需要信任NVidia等硬件供应商，可能存在后门风险。
• [rkagerer] 关注收入模式，质疑该平台是否能抵抗云供应商直接复制其技术并提供相似服务。他还提到开源代码（AGPL）的潜在影响，并询问该平台的“秘密武器”是什么。
• [madars] 提到该方案可以避免模型对用户输入的过度“对齐”限制，例如Anthropic或OpenAI对查询的过滤和审查。他认为开放模型应像水电一样，供应商只提供基础能力，使用责任由用户承担。

补充讨论：
• [kevinis] 提到GPU服务器的物理位置问题，询问它们是否位于美国，以及是否自建数据中心或租用大型云供应商的服务器。
• [internetter] 质疑可信执行环境（enclave）如何确保不会声称运行旧的代码版本。
• [SebP] 分享了自己正在开发的一个类似项目，强调了“可验证安全”的重要性，并提到使用开放源LLM和RAG（检索增强生成）技术。
• [gojomo] 询问是否存在一个可以被审计的固定客户端，以确保用户只需信任硬件设计和制造商，而不是每次使用时都需要信任服务提供商的动态代码。

争议的焦点：
• 该产品与苹果公司“私有云计算”方案的区别和独特性。
• 硬件信任根和潜在的漏洞问题。
• 是否过度依赖信任，尤其是在涉及敏感数据时。
• 大型云供应商是否会很快进入并主导这一市场。

data.title: Show HN: Goboscript, text-based programming language, compiles to Scratch
data.author: aspizu
data.article_summary: goboscript 是一种基于文本的编程语言，能够编译为 Scratch 项目（.sb3 文件），允许在文本编辑器中编写 Scratch 代码，并支持版本控制和代码复用。它具有简洁易读的语法，支持宏系统和额外功能（如局部变量），并可集成外部工具和工作流。goboscript 还提供优化和问题检测功能。开发者可以通过克隆项目并在本地运行，使用特定脚本进行编译、验证、提取和修补 Scratch 项目。该项目在 FOSS HACK 25  hackathon 中获得一等奖及50,000卢比奖励，使用 Rust 编写，并欢迎社区贡献。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Scratch编程教学及其过渡到文本编程的挑战与可能性

不同观点：
• AlexanderDhoore认为，Scratch是一个很好的入门工具，但孩子们在掌握Scratch后会遇到多重障碍，尤其是向文本编程过渡时的语言、计算机概念和打字问题。他建议在Scratch生态系统内逐步引入更多概念，使过渡更平滑，并提到GoboScript作为一种可能的解决方案，但他更希望引入Python或JavaScript等真实编程语言。
• varun_ch从自身经验出发，强调Scratch不仅是一个拖放式编程工具，还是一个包含社区和可扩展性的生态系统。他指出，通过“破解”Scratch可以学到很多东西，且Scratch设计者也意识到并鼓励这种学习方式。
• japanuspus对项目表示感谢，但指出安装说明的缺乏可能成为新手用户的障碍，建议增加简单的安装指引以提高可访问性。
• falcor84提到pytch.org作为一个类似解决方案，可以在Python中重现Scratch的功能，并建议结合两种方法。
• nis251413建议创建一个编译到GoboScript的可视化编程语言。
• ferriswil对项目表示赞赏，并提出构建非Scratch运行时和类似Scratch前端的需求，以教授低龄儿童自举概念。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者如arjvik和sriram_malhar对项目表示赞赏，并提到项目带来的怀旧感和功能改进。
• ninetyninenine和web3aj对向文本编程过渡的必要性提出质疑，认为Scratch本身已经足够，并对项目的目的提出质疑。

争议焦点：
• 是否需要从Scratch过渡到文本编程以及如何实现这种过渡是讨论的核心争议点。一方认为过渡是必要的且需要简化，另一方则认为Scratch本身已经足够有效，不需要强行过渡。

总结：评论主要围绕Scratch编程教学的效果及如何帮助学生过渡到文本编程展开，涉及具体工具和方法的建议以及对过渡必要性的不同看法。

goboscript
Installation and documentation
goboscript is a text-based programming language which compiles to Scratch. It allows
you to write Scratch projects in text, and compile it into a .sb3 file - which can be
opened in the Scratch editor, TurboWarp or be uploaded to the Scratch website.
goboscript allows you to create advanced Scratch projects with ease, you can use any
text editor, use a version control system such as git. You can refactor your code
using search and replace. Text code can be copy pasted, which allows you to easily reuse
code or share it with others. goboscript syntax is concise and easy to read.
goboscript allows you to integrate external tooling and workflows, such as using a
script to generate costumes for a text rendering engine. Or loading in images into
lists.
goboscript has a powerful macro system - similar to Rust's macro system. This allows
you to write macros to generate code.
goboscript is more than just an 1:1 mapping of Scratch blocks to text, it also has
additional features like local variables for procedures (custom blocks).
goboscript also performs optimizations, detects problems and unused code.
Sister Projects
Package Manager
Decompiler
Contributing
goboscript welcomes contributions in the form of Pull Requests.
goboscript is written in Rust. You'll need to install the
Rust toolchain
for development.
Note
To install goboscript, follow instructions at
aspizu.github.io/goboscript
.
These instructions are for people who want to develop goboscript itself.
git clone https://github.com/aspizu/goboscript
cd
goboscript
Development
After cloning the repository, run goboscript locally from the repository root with:
cargo run -- build -i your_project/
But, to make development easier, and to validate the generated Scratch project - use
the
tools/run
script:
tools/run compile
This assumes that you have set-up a testing project at
playground/
.
It will compile the project, validate it using the schemas from
scratch-parser
.
If the validation fails, Scratch will refuse to load the project. To further debug
the project, the generated
project.json
file is extracted from the
.sb3
file in the
playground/
directory.
Lets say that you modified the generated project in the Scratch editor or Turbowarp,
and you want to look at the
project.json
. You can extract it with:
tools/run uncompile
Lets say that goboscript produced a broken project, and you are able to fix it by hand -
by modifying the
project.json
. You can add back the
project.json
to the
.sb3
file
with:
tools/run patch
If you want to validate some
.sb3
file, use:
tools/run check path/to/project.sb3

44026799.article_summary: goboscript 是一种基于文本的编程语言，能够编译为 Scratch 项目（.sb3 文件），允许在文本编辑器中编写 Scratch 代码，并支持版本控制和代码复用。它具有简洁易读的语法，支持宏系统和额外功能（如局部变量），并可集成外部工具和工作流。goboscript 还提供优化和问题检测功能。开发者可以通过克隆项目并在本地运行，使用特定脚本进行编译、验证、提取和修补 Scratch 项目。该项目在 FOSS HACK 25  hackathon 中获得一等奖及50,000卢比奖励，使用 Rust 编写，并欢迎社区贡献。

主要讨论点：Scratch编程教学及其过渡到文本编程的挑战与可能性

不同观点：
• AlexanderDhoore认为，Scratch是一个很好的入门工具，但孩子们在掌握Scratch后会遇到多重障碍，尤其是向文本编程过渡时的语言、计算机概念和打字问题。他建议在Scratch生态系统内逐步引入更多概念，使过渡更平滑，并提到GoboScript作为一种可能的解决方案，但他更希望引入Python或JavaScript等真实编程语言。
• varun_ch从自身经验出发，强调Scratch不仅是一个拖放式编程工具，还是一个包含社区和可扩展性的生态系统。他指出，通过“破解”Scratch可以学到很多东西，且Scratch设计者也意识到并鼓励这种学习方式。
• japanuspus对项目表示感谢，但指出安装说明的缺乏可能成为新手用户的障碍，建议增加简单的安装指引以提高可访问性。
• falcor84提到pytch.org作为一个类似解决方案，可以在Python中重现Scratch的功能，并建议结合两种方法。
• nis251413建议创建一个编译到GoboScript的可视化编程语言。
• ferriswil对项目表示赞赏，并提出构建非Scratch运行时和类似Scratch前端的需求，以教授低龄儿童自举概念。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论者如arjvik和sriram_malhar对项目表示赞赏，并提到项目带来的怀旧感和功能改进。
• ninetyninenine和web3aj对向文本编程过渡的必要性提出质疑，认为Scratch本身已经足够，并对项目的目的提出质疑。

争议焦点：
• 是否需要从Scratch过渡到文本编程以及如何实现这种过渡是讨论的核心争议点。一方认为过渡是必要的且需要简化，另一方则认为Scratch本身已经足够有效，不需要强行过渡。

总结：评论主要围绕Scratch编程教学的效果及如何帮助学生过渡到文本编程展开，涉及具体工具和方法的建议以及对过渡必要性的不同看法。

data.title: The principles of database design, or, the Truth is out there
data.author: b-man
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了数据库设计的基本原则，强调数据库必须准确反映现实世界的业务逻辑。数据库设计无法完全自动化，需要人工编码以确保语义正确。文章列出了几项关键原则，如正交设计原则（POOD）、表示简约原则（PORP）、表达完整性原则（POEC）、完全规范化原则（POFN）和信息原则（TIP），并引入了一个新原则——本质指示原则（PED），主张使用自然键而非代理键来标识实体。错误的设计会导致数据不一致和更新异常，带来严重后果。良好的数据库设计需要严格的纪律和对基础原则的掌握，以确保信息的准确性和系统的稳定性。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：是否应使用自然键作为数据库实体的主键，或是否应采用代理键（如UUID、自增ID等）

不同观点：
• **支持代理键（adamcharnock, exabrial, pretoriusdre, peanut-walrus, RedShift1）**  
  - 代理键更灵活，适用于多种用途（如连接、查找、索引），并且在性能和资源使用上更优。
  - 自然键可能会变化，例如身份盗用或政府重新分配ID时，管理起来非常复杂。
  - 自然键不一定是唯一的，例如美国的社会安全号码（SSN）有重复的情况。
  - 使用自然键可能导致数据迁移问题，例如电话号码或国家ID格式变化时的痛苦迁移经历。
  - 建议不要将外部分配的标识符用作主键，而是使用简单的整数作为代理键，并通过唯一约束保证自然键的唯一性。

• **支持自然键（jandrewrogers, photios, stevoski）**  
  - 在某些领域中，自然键可能不存在或需要通过推理得出，数据模型需要处理这种不确定性。
  - 自然键在某些情况下是不可靠的，例如国家ID可能会有重复或变更，但在某些场景下仍然具有实际意义。
  - 有些人可能没有国家ID，或不愿意提供，因此需要灵活处理现实中的数据不一致问题。

• **对自然键与代理键的折中态度（AnonHP, madduci, weinzierl）**  
  - 强调数据库设计需要根据实际需求权衡，而非一味追求最高范式或理论上的完美设计。
  - 不同应用场景可能需要不同的数据存储结构，可能导致数据重复，但在性能和报告需求下是可接受的折中。
  - 某些ORM库（如Java JPA）不支持复杂的自然键管理，因此开发者倾向于使用代理键和代码管理实体，但这可能导致优化问题。

补充讨论：
- 有评论指出，某些数据模型的身份识别本质上是一个推断问题，无法明确界定自然键（jandrewrogers）。
- 一些评论提到数据库设计需要考虑现实硬件和操作环境的限制，而不仅是理论上的理想模型（jandrewrogers, RedShift1）。
- 最高范式（如3NF、BCNF等）并非总是最佳选择，有时为了性能需要做出权衡（weinzierl, AnonHP）。
- 自然键的变化和不确定性可能导致实际应用中的复杂性，尤其是在跨系统共享和ID生成时（adamcharnock, exabrial）。

争议焦点：自然键的唯一性、可变性以及在实际应用中的管理复杂性，与代理键的性能优势和简化管理之间的权衡。

44026201.article_content:
The principles of database design, or,  the Truth is out there
May 17, 2025
by Eduardo Bellani
Every software project needs to represent the reality of the business he
is embedded in. The way we can represent reality as limited rational
beings is through propositions, i.e, declarative statements that affirm
or deny something about reality. When a collection of such propositions
is stored in a computer system, we call it a database.
Such database needs to be designed to properly reflect reality. This
can’t be automated, since the semantics of the situation need to be
encoded in a way that can be processed by a computer. Such then is the
goal of database design: to encode propositions in such a way that can
properly be processed by a database management system (DBMS).
At this point, a regular software developer comes to a stall. Since
there is scarcely any formal training in database design (or formal
logic) in his education, he tends to fall back haphazardly on ad-hoc
methods, with severe consequences (update anomalies and data
inconsitencies with huge potential downsides).
If you are such developer, you
need
to understand the underlying
principles of database design. Think about it, if you don’t have
principles of design, you are not doing engineering, are you?
Here is a list of design principles to follow for formal database
design(
McGoveran 2012
,
2015
)(
Pascal 2016
):
Principle of Orthogonal Design (POOD): Base relations are independent;
Principle of Representational Parsimony (PORP): There are no
superfluous base relations;
Principle of Expressive Completeness (POEC): All meaningful relations
are derivable from the base relations.
Principle of Full Normalization (POFN) : Every base relation should be
in its highest normal form (3, 5 or 6th normal form).​ Thus eliminating
redundancy and preventing anomalies by ensuring that each relation is
free from undesirable characteristics like partial, transitive, or
join dependencies.
The Information Principle (TIP) : All information in the database is
represented explicitly and in exactly one way — by attribute values
drawn from domains in relations.
Principle of Logical Independence (PLI) : Application programs and
terminal activities remain logically unimpaired when information
preserving changes of any kind that theoretically permit unimpairment
are made to the base relations.
To these I’d like to introduce a new principle, an innovation I hope to
develop in future work:
Principle of Essential Denotation (PED): A relation should be
identified by a natural key that reflects the entity’s essential,
domain-defined identity — not by arbitrary or surrogate values.
The following pseudo-SQL shows the contrast between improper and proper denotation:
-- usage of surrogate keys
create
table
citizen
(
id
uuid
primary
key
,
national_id
text
,
full_name
text
);
Code Snippet 1:
Illustration of not using PED with SQL
This usage has some problems, the worst of it is the disconnection
between database structure and domain semantics. Here is a rework that
preserves such connection:
create
domain
national_id
as
text
check
(...);
create
table
citizen
(
national_id
national_id
primary
key
,
full_name
text
);
Code Snippet 2:
Illustration of using PED with SQL
Conclusion
Databases are representations of reality, and as such, they are
foundational to any serious information system. Poor design leads to
semantic confusion and technical instability—with consequences that can
be costly and far-reaching. Good design demands rigor, discipline, and a
firm grasp of foundational principles.
To put it simply: if you’re in the business of information, you need to
know how to build structures that tell the truth that is out there.
References
Blakemore, Erin. 2019. “The Notre-Dame Cathedral Was Nearly Destroyed by French Revolutionary Mobs (Accessed on 2025-05-18).”
https://web.archive.org/web/20190607211856/https://www.history.com/news/notre-dame-fire-french-revolution
.
McGoveran, David. 2012. “Updating a Database.” Alternative Technologies Blog.
http://w.alternativetech.com/publications/View%20Updating%206-12-12.pdf
.
———. 2015. “Can All Relations Be Updated? (or Can Any Relation Be Updated?) Logic for Serious Database Folks Series.” Alternative Technologies Blog.
https://www.alternativetech.com/publications/Logic%20for%20DB%20Folks%20Series%20XX%20-%20Updating%20Relations.pdf
.
Pascal, Fabian. 2016. “The Principle of Orthogonal Database Design Part I.”
https://www.dbdebunk.com/2016/09/the-principle-of-orthogonal-database.html
.

data.title: Layers All the Way Down: The Untold Story of Shader Compilation
data.author: birdculture
data.article_summary:
本文讨论了跨平台图形渲染中的主要挑战，尤其是不同硬件加速API（如Vulkan、Metal、D3D11等）的差异带来的复杂性。作者是FNA项目的共同维护者，该项目旨在将XNA框架适配到现代平台。作者开发了FNA3D图形抽象库，并创建了Refresh API，试图通过统一的架构简化多平台渲染问题。Refresh允许开发者提交SPIR-V或特定后端的高级语言及字节码来创建着色器对象，以解决不同图形API的兼容性问题。

文章还解释了着色器的基本概念及其演变。早期图形API为固定功能，后来引入可编程着色器阶段，允许更多渲染灵活性。现代API通常使用字节码而非实时编译的高级语言，以减少驱动程序的复杂性和计算开销。然而，GPU的硬件多样性使得统一的着色器编译标准难以实现，不同制造商的GPU具有各自独特的指令集和要求，增加了开发难度。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕图形渲染、着色器编译及其在不同平台上的实现和支持的讨论。

不同观点：
• **raphlinus的观点**：提到piet-gpu-hal项目中使用SPIRV-cross的不足，比如在Metal 3.2之前设备范围屏障会被忽略，以及原子操作的问题。他还指出着色器语言本身不是主要问题，而是绑定模型，尤其是在无绑定（bindless）方向上的变化。他提到了不同的解决方案，包括WebGPU的重构和Dzmitry Malyshau的Blade项目，但认为这是一条艰难的道路。

• **riggsdk的观点**：介绍了BGFX的另一种方法，使用类似GLSL的语言，并通过宏扩展处理平台差异，从而支持OpenGL、WebGL、Vulkan、Metal等多种后端。这种方法依赖于各平台自带的着色器编译器，进行最小程度的源代码转换。

• **pornel的观点**：对WebGPU API表示赞赏，认为它是主要平台厂商合作的产物，并在所有主要平台上有实际实现。他还指出wgpu和Google dawn的实现使WebGPU API不仅限于Web，还可以用于本地应用程序。

• **shmerl的观点**：批评GPU API领域的“非我发明”（NIH）心态，指出由于锁园政策，Vulkan在某些平台上得不到支持。他认为微软决定使用SPIR-V并最终放弃DXIL是一个小的积极进展，但还不够。

• **voidUpdate的观点**：质疑为何在需要实时编译着色器的情况下，Unreal引擎需要花费很长时间编译大量着色器，影响用户体验。

• **mvdtnz的观点**：对游戏需要频繁编译着色器表示不解，并提出为何游戏不能像Steam一样在后台或空闲时间自动更新和编译着色器，以节省用户时间。

补充讨论：

44026170.article_content:
Layers All The Way Down: The Untold Story of Shader Compilation
ï¬
2024-07-01
Background
As a game developer who works primarily in frameworks instead of engines, one of the biggest pain points is the need to render on multiple platforms efficiently. For most platform-level tasks, like window management, input handling, etc,
SDL
does a beautiful job and I barely have to think about it.
Rendering, by comparison, is a huge can of worms. Every platform has their own unique support matrix. For Windows you have D3D12/D3D11/Vulkan/OpenGL. For Apple platforms you have Metal and OpenGL, or OpenGL ES if you’re on iOS/tvOS. For Linux and Nintendo you have Vulkan and OpenGL. For PlayStation you have whatever the hell they have going on over there. For Xbox you have D3D12 only. Android has Vulkan and OpenGL ES. You get the picture.
All of these hardware acceleration APIs have similarities, but they have enough differences that mapping all the functionality you need onto them is nontrivial.
I am a co-maintainer of the
FNA project
, which is a project that preserves the XNA framework on contemporary platforms. As part of this work for a few years I have worked on our cross-platform graphics abstraction
FNA3D
, particularly on the Vulkan implementation. This library allows us to translate XNA graphics calls to modern systems.
My work on that project led me to create
Refresh
, which has a similar architecture but is influenced by the structure of Vulkan and modernized in several key regards. For the past several months I have been working on submitting a version of that API as a
proposal to SDL
. Ryan C. Gordon (aka icculus) announced plans to include a GPU API in SDL a few years ago. Refresh only differed from his proposal in a few small details, and the implementation was mostly complete, so the FNA team submitted what I had written in the hopes of saving some time and developer effort.
For the most part this has been fairly well-received, but there is a question we have been asked repeatedly. Presently we support Vulkan, Metal, and D3D11, with other backends coming soon. In our API, to create a shader object you must submit either SPIR-V which we transpile at runtime, a high-level language supported by a specific backend, or bytecode supported by a specific backend. Why did we decide to structure things this way? To answer this question I will try to explain some of the technical and political challenges in today’s graphics landscape.
What
is
a shader?
In Ye Olde Days, graphics APIs consisted of function entry points that would map to dedicated hardware logic. This was known as a fixed-function API. OpenGL was a fixed-function API until version 2, and Direct3D until version 8. You had the functions these APIs provided for modulating data, and that was it.
With the advent of GL2 and D3D8, the concept of a programmable shader stage was introduced. This allowed a much larger range of rendering flexibility.
A shader is effectively a massively-parallel program that is executed on the GPU. The task of a shader is to transform large amounts of data in parallel. A vertex shader takes in vertex data and transforms each vertex in parallel. A fragment shader takes transformed information from the vertex shader and the hardware rasterization process to output a color value to each rasterized pixel in parallel. A compute shader transforms more-or-less arbitrary data in parallel.
In Ye Slightly Less Olde Days, these APIs would take in high-level shader programs. You would write shader code in text format, pass that to the API, and it would attempt to compile the shader at runtime. This approach had some significant drawbacks: this meant that driver authors had to ship entire compilers in their drivers, and parsing and compiling requires a nontrivial amount of computation time, which is awkward especially when you’re trying to hit 16ms per frame or minimize up-front load times. This also meant that if the driver had a compiler bug, you would only find out at runtime on a specific install. Yikes! In contemporary APIs, you instead pass bytecode (or intermediate representation) to the driver, which cuts out a lot of the complexity. However, these bytecode programs still have to be compiled into a natively-executable format.
Let’s back up a little. Programming languages are very abstracted these days, so it’s easy to forget that the programs have to be transformed into actual machine code to be executed. Consider the two common CPU instruction sets, x86 and ARM. These have become so standard that most of us take it for granted that basically every CPU is going to use one or the other. When you compile a program, you compile it to one or the other, and you have support on the vast majority of actual hardware.
GPUs are not an exception to the fact that programs have to run on actual hardware. Where x86 and ARM have won the instruction set wars in CPU-land, the situation with GPUs is not even remotely this standardized.

44026170.article_summary:
本文讨论了跨平台图形渲染中的主要挑战，尤其是不同硬件加速API（如Vulkan、Metal、D3D11等）的差异带来的复杂性。作者是FNA项目的共同维护者，该项目旨在将XNA框架适配到现代平台。作者开发了FNA3D图形抽象库，并创建了Refresh API，试图通过统一的架构简化多平台渲染问题。Refresh允许开发者提交SPIR-V或特定后端的高级语言及字节码来创建着色器对象，以解决不同图形API的兼容性问题。

文章还解释了着色器的基本概念及其演变。早期图形API为固定功能，后来引入可编程着色器阶段，允许更多渲染灵活性。现代API通常使用字节码而非实时编译的高级语言，以减少驱动程序的复杂性和计算开销。然而，GPU的硬件多样性使得统一的着色器编译标准难以实现，不同制造商的GPU具有各自独特的指令集和要求，增加了开发难度。
44026170.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕图形渲染、着色器编译及其在不同平台上的实现和支持的讨论。

不同观点：
• **raphlinus的观点**：提到piet-gpu-hal项目中使用SPIRV-cross的不足，比如在Metal 3.2之前设备范围屏障会被忽略，以及原子操作的问题。他还指出着色器语言本身不是主要问题，而是绑定模型，尤其是在无绑定（bindless）方向上的变化。他提到了不同的解决方案，包括WebGPU的重构和Dzmitry Malyshau的Blade项目，但认为这是一条艰难的道路。

• **riggsdk的观点**：介绍了BGFX的另一种方法，使用类似GLSL的语言，并通过宏扩展处理平台差异，从而支持OpenGL、WebGL、Vulkan、Metal等多种后端。这种方法依赖于各平台自带的着色器编译器，进行最小程度的源代码转换。

• **pornel的观点**：对WebGPU API表示赞赏，认为它是主要平台厂商合作的产物，并在所有主要平台上有实际实现。他还指出wgpu和Google dawn的实现使WebGPU API不仅限于Web，还可以用于本地应用程序。

• **shmerl的观点**：批评GPU API领域的“非我发明”（NIH）心态，指出由于锁园政策，Vulkan在某些平台上得不到支持。他认为微软决定使用SPIR-V并最终放弃DXIL是一个小的积极进展，但还不够。

• **voidUpdate的观点**：质疑为何在需要实时编译着色器的情况下，Unreal引擎需要花费很长时间编译大量着色器，影响用户体验。

• **mvdtnz的观点**：对游戏需要频繁编译着色器表示不解，并提出为何游戏不能像Steam一样在后台或空闲时间自动更新和编译着色器，以节省用户时间。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：不同平台和API之间的着色器编译和支持问题，以及如何优化着色器编译过程以减少对用户体验的影响。

data.title: The lack of a good command line way to sort IPv6 addresses
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文解释了为何一些用户在访问博客"Wandering Thoughts"或其所属的CSpace时被阻止。原因是这些用户使用的浏览器版本过旧，被网站的反爬虫机制误认为是用于数据爬取的恶意爬虫，尤其是用于LLM训练的高 volume 爬虫。这种情况常见于旧版Chrome浏览器。若用户确实在使用当前浏览器版本而被误拦截，可联系作者。特别提到，使用archive.*服务（如archive.today, archive.ph）的用户也可能遇到此问题，因为这些服务使用的旧Chrome用户代理和分布广泛的IP地址，类似恶意爬虫行为。建议使用更规范的archive.org进行存档。作者为造成的不便表示歉意，并希望用户提供浏览器信息以改进机制。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：如何对IPv6地址进行排序，以及IPv4到IPv6迁移中的概念差异和排序实现方法

不同观点：
• miyuru：认为IP版本的设计初衷并不包含排序功能，排序只是地址表示形式带来的副产品。同时指出，IPv4的概念不能直接应用于IPv6，这也是IPv6难以部署的原因之一。直接将IPv4的思路套用到IPv6上会导致相同的问题。
• ggm：提出了一种具体的排序方法，通过将IP地址转换为不压缩零的十六进制字符串进行排序，然后再转换回来。这种方法需要对前缀/长度进行特殊处理。
• schoen：提供了一种使用Python实现IPv6地址排序的代码示例，通过`ipaddress`库对地址进行排序，并可以选择在排序后重新压缩地址表示。
• wpm：对使用十六进制表示IP地址的方式提出质疑，认为这可能不是一个好主意。
• fragmede：建议编写一个名为`sort6`的工具来专门处理IPv6地址的排序问题，认为这是标准化做法。
• 0points：提出了一种简单的三步方法：转换为数字表示、排序、再转换回来。

补充讨论：
• sargstuff：详细讨论了如何将IPv6地址规范化为可排序的格式，引用了RFC 5952中推荐的规范文本表示法。还提出了一些具体的技术方法，如使用正则表达式或`sprintf`格式化、转换为'可排序的UTF-16字符'、以及利用Python库处理IPv4/IPv6地址的排序问题，并提供了一些参考链接。

争议焦点：
• IPv6地址排序的最佳实践和工具实现方式存在不同看法。
• 直接将IPv4的概念应用于IPv6是否可行，以及这样做会带来的问题。

总体来看，讨论围绕IPv6地址排序的技术实现展开，涉及具体的方法、工具建议以及对IPv4与IPv6之间概念差异的讨论。

You're using a suspiciously old browser
You're probably reading this page because you've attempted to access
some part of
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
or
CSpace
, the wiki thing it's part of. Unfortunately
you're using a browser version that my anti-crawler precautions consider
suspicious, most often because it's too old (most often this applies to
versions of Chrome). Unfortunately, as of early 2025 there's a plague
of high volume crawlers (apparently in part to gather data for LLM
training) that use a variety of old browser user agents, especially
Chrome user agents. To reduce the load on
Wandering Thoughts
I'm experimenting with
(attempting to) block all of them, and you've run into this.
If this is in error and you're using a current version of your
browser of choice, you can contact me at
my current place at the
university
(you should be able to work out the email address
from that). If possible, please let me know what browser you're
using and so on, ideally with its exactl User-Agent string.
A special note for people using archive.*
You may be seeing this through archive.today, archive.ph, archive.is,
and so on. Unfortunately, archive.* crawls pages to archive in a way that
is impossible to distinguish from malicious actors. They use old Chrome
User-Agent values, crawl from IP address blocks that are widely distributed
and not clearly identified as theirs, and some of their IP addresses have
falsified reverse DNS entries that claim they are googlebot IP addresses
(which is something that is normally done only by quite bad actors). I
suggest that you use archive.org, which is a better behaved archival
crawler and can crawl
my blog (Wandering Thoughts)
.
Chris Siebenmann, 2025-02-17

Publisher是一个开源的语义模型服务器，用于Malloy数据建模语言。Malloy是一种开源语言，用于构建丰富的语义数据模型，定义数据的意义、关系和背景。Publisher通过服务器接口公开这些语义模型，使应用程序、AI代理、工具和用户能够一致可靠地查询数据。其目标是解决现代数据和AI系统中数据意义不明确的问题，确保不同工具和代理对数据有一致的理解，从而获得可信的答案。

Publisher主要包括三个组件：Publisher Server（API和后端）、Publisher SDK（UI组件）和Publisher App（参考数据应用实现）。Publisher Server是核心后端，负责加载和管理Malloy包，使用Malloy运行时解析和编译Malloy查询为SQL，支持多种数据库。API层包括REST API和Model Context Protocol (MCP) API，用于不同客户端交互和查询执行。Publisher提供了一种开放源码、以开发者为中心的方式来定义、管理和提供语义层，确保数据访问的一致性和可解释性。

Publisher: The Malloy Semantic Model Server
Welcome to Publisher, the open-source semantic model server for the
Malloy
data language.
What is Malloy?
Malloy
is a open-source language for modeling data. Malloy allows you to build rich
semantic data models
– defining the
meaning
,
relationships
, and
context
behind your datas.
Malloy provides a robust framework to encode the business context of your data and running queries against your databases. The accompanying
VS Code extension
provides an environment for developing Malloy models, exploring data, and building simple dashboards.
What is Publisher?
Publisher takes the semantic models defined in Malloy – models rich with business context and meaning – and exposes them through a server interface. This allows applications,
AI agents
, tools, and users to query your data consistently and reliably, leveraging the shared, unambiguous understanding defined in the Malloy model.
The Goal:
Publisher solves a growing problem in modern data and AI systems: You can’t trust answers if the meaning behind the data isn’t clear.
Whether it’s a dashboard, a data app, or an AI-agent, every application that interacts with your data needs to understand what terms like "revenue", "active user", or "churn" actually mean in your business. Without that shared understanding, answers are inconsistent at best — and dangerously wrong at worst.
Publisher serves semantic models — defined in Malloy — via APIs. This means:
You query data in terms of your business, not raw SQL.
Tools and agents make API calls using Malloy queries, and Publisher compiles them to SQL behind the scenes.
You get trusted answers from your agent, dashboard, or embedded app — without redefining you data's meaning in every tool.
We believe the semantic layer is the missing keystone of the modern data stack. Publisher and Malloy provide an open-source, developer-first way to define, manage, and serve that layer — enabling consistent, interpretable, and AI-ready data access across all your tools.
Instead of locking your definitions into proprietary BI platforms, you can now ship them like code: versioned, tested, and served through clean interfaces.
Architecture Overview
Publisher consists of three main components: the Publisher Server (APIs & backend, now including MCP support), the Publisher SDK (UI components), and the Publisher App (a reference data app implementation).
The image below illustrates the composition of the Publisher's components and the tools & applications it can support.
1. Publisher Server (
packages/server/
)
Core Backend:
This is the heart of Publisher. It's a server application responsible for loading and managing Malloy Packages, which encapsulate your semantic models.
Malloy Integration:
It utilizes the Malloy runtime to parse
.malloy
files, understand the rich semantic models defined within them (including relationships, calculations, and business context), and compile Malloy queries into SQL for execution against target databases (BigQuery, Snowflake, Trino, DuckDB, Postgres, MySQL).
API Layers:
The Publisher server exposes two primary API interfaces (with one more coming soon:
REST API:

, default
4000
)

localhost
)

Used by the web frontend (Publisher App/SDK) for browsing packages, models, and executing queries.

.

None.

data.title: Llama from scratch (2023)
data.author: sebg
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何从零开始实现一个简化版的Llama模型，用于训练TinyShakespeare数据集。作者分享了实现过程中的经验和技巧，强调了迭代工作的重要性：从小处着手，逐步构建和验证模型。具体步骤包括：

Takeaways
Always work iteratively: start small, stay certain, and build up.
My approach for implementing papers is:
Make all of the helper functions required to test your model quantitatively (data splits, training, plotting the loss).
Before you even look at the paper, pick a small, simple, and fast model that you've done in the past. Then make a helper function to evaluate the model qualitatively.
Start by picking apart different components of the paper, and then implementing them one-by-one, training and evaluating as you go.
Make sure your layers do what you think.
Use

and
plt.imshow
are also your friends.
Work out the results without matrix multiplication first, and then use the
torch
